title: Shetland-style triangle with shell border
subtitle: A treble lace body with a shell-stitch border, inspired by Shetland shawl construction, in natural grey DK
excerpt: This triangular shawl draws on Shetland shawl construction: a lace body worked from the centre out with a deep shell-stitch border applied separately around all three edges. The body is an openwork treble lace in DK weight natural grey on a 4 mm hook. The border adds approximately 8 cm of depth to each edge. Finished size is 145 cm wide by 68 cm deep. Requires confident lace counting and border pick-up.
sourceNotes: Construction inspired by traditional Shetland shawl technique, documented in Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 2 and 3 (1886-1887), which describe lace-body shawls with applied shell borders (Internet Archive). Lace body structure adapted from de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A shawl-making method where the centre body and border are worked separately and then joined, or the border is picked up and worked outward from the body edge. In this crochet version the shell border is worked directly into the body edge stitches and row ends.

A border worked onto a finished piece by picking up into the edge stitches and row ends rather than being worked as part of the fabric from the start. Gives a clean transition between the body lace and the border pattern.

content.text: Traditional Shetland shawls separate the centre body from the border: the body uses one stitch pattern and the border uses a different, often denser one. This crochet interpretation uses the same principle. The lace body is a V-stitch grid (one treble, ch 2, skip 2, repeat) that produces an open, lightweight fabric. The
applied border
is a five-treble shell worked directly into the edge stitches of the finished body.
This is an advanced pattern because it requires consistent lace tension throughout a large piece and accurate border pick-up along both diagonal edges. The
Shetland construction
means the shawl is always blocked in two stages: once for the body before the border, and again for the finished piece.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 450 g DK-weight yarn in natural grey. A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers (at least 3). Blocking mat. Rust-proof pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

18 tr x 10 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook, measured over plain treble fabric after blocking. The lace body will be slightly more open than a plain treble swatch; the gauge measurement is used as a reference for the border spacing.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
shell: 5 tr into the same stitch or chain space.
Pattern
The shawl is worked in two parts: the lace body first, then the shell border.
Part 1: Lace body
Foundation ring
Ch 5. Sl st to form a ring. Place a stitch marker in the ring.
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 5 (counts as tr + ch 2). 1 tr in ring. Ch 2. 1 tr in ring (spine). Ch 2. 1 tr in ring. Ch 2. 1 tr in ring. Turn. (4 tr, 3 ch-2 spaces)
Row 2 (increase row)

Ch 5 (counts as tr + ch 2). *1 tr in next tr. Ch 2*; repeat from * to * across. Into the spine tr work: (1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr, ch 2, 1 tr), which is the spine increase. Continue *ch 2. 1 tr in next tr*; to end. Ch 2. 1 tr in 3rd ch of turning ch. Turn. (one extra tr-ch-2 unit added at each edge)
Rows 3 to approximately 60

Repeat Row 2 on every row. After approximately 60 rows the body measures approximately 127 cm wide (before the border) and 60 cm deep. Fasten off. Block the body at this stage: wet-block to the stated pre-border dimensions and allow to dry fully before working the border.
Part 2: Shell border
The shell border is worked in two passes around the two diagonal edges only. The straight top edge is finished with dc only.

Round 1 (preparation): join yarn at the top right corner. Work 1 dc into each row-end tr and 1 dc into each ch-2 space along the right diagonal edge to the bottom point. At the bottom point work (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc) into the corner stitch. Continue up the left diagonal edge in the same way. Along the top straight edge, work 1 dc into each tr and ch-2 space. Join with sl st.

Round 2 (shell round): do not work along the top edge. Work along the two diagonal edges only. *Skip 2 dc. 5 tr in next dc (shell). Skip 2 dc. 1 sl st in next dc*; repeat from * to * along both diagonal edges. At the bottom corner ch-2 space, work (5 tr, ch 2, 5 tr) into the space to turn the corner. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends. Wet-block the completed shawl including the border: pin to 145 x 68 cm on a blocking mat, easing the shell border to lie flat and opening the lace body to full width.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Lay flat to dry. Re-block lightly after each wash to keep the lace body and shell border at full width.
What to try next

Work the border in a contrast colour for a clear separation between body and border. A double shell border (two rounds of shells rather than one) adds more depth along the edges. For a finer piece, work the same construction in fingering weight on a 3.25 mm hook.
